title: What had I already accepted? (worked out on cardboard)
note: The authored thinking for one hall, in the first person, by the pass (Claude), for Palle's request of 2026-11-14 (see Russell_Paradox.json). 'at' is the floor's own frame in metres (x east, z south), 'yaw' in degrees. A sticker of kind 'quote' stands word for word in the hall text; every other kind is mine and may be wrong - the plates say where I am unsure.

hero.why: The plaque is where the five things to grant are listed and where one of them can be lit and un-lit. Everything on this floor is about the difference between lighting an assumption and holding it.
hero.staging: The plaque hangs straight ahead of the arrival with a ring under it. Plates 1 and 2 stand at either hand; the threads run north past the hall's lines and triangle to the lane where the fifth is laid out the length of the slab.

plates.title: 1  WHAT I HAD ALREADY ACCEPTED
front: I have drawn triangles all the way down this tower and never asked what I agreed to in order to draw one.
Euclid lists five things to grant. Four sound like permissions: join two points, extend a line, draw a circle, all right angles are equal.
The fifth is a sentence about what two lines will do far away, where nobody is looking.
It reads like a result. It is asked for like a favour.
So: which of my 'obviously' are favours I stopped noticing I asked for?
back: I am going from memory for the wording of the first four. the plaque has them. read the plaque, not me.

plates.title: 2  GOLD REMOVES THE EMPHASIS, NOT THE ASSUMPTION
front: On the plaque GOLD lights the fifth. Press it again: the gold goes, the sentence stays.
I expected un-highlighting to feel like removing. It removes nothing.
An assumption does not need to be marked to be in force. Mostly it is in force BECAUSE it is not marked.
To take it out I would have to change what the lines do - not how the plaque looks.
(That is the next floor.)
back: highlighting is a thing done to readers. assuming is a thing done to lines.

plates.title: 3  PARALLEL IS NOT EVENLY SPACED
front: Three line modules. Unequal gaps, same direction.
My eye wanted 'parallel' to mean 'a regular pattern'. It means: these do not meet.
That is a claim about everywhere along them. It is checked nowhere.
Equal gaps I can measure, here. Never meeting I cannot measure anywhere.
So parallel is a word I cannot confirm by looking.
back: I wanted to write 'the FIRST such word in this tower'. it is not: 'random', a hundred floors up, could not be confirmed by looking either.

plates.title: 4  THE LABELS SAY SIXTY. THE CORNERS DO NOT
front: The small triangle carries three labels: 60, 60, 60. Its drawn corners are plainly not equal.
The numbers were supplied. Nobody measured.
I believed the labels before I looked at the corners. I always believe the label first.
Three kinds of thing stand in this room and look alike: what is given, what is measured, what follows.
The labels are given. The tutorial's angles are measured. 180 follows - if the fifth is granted.
back: which of the three is this cardboard? given. nobody measured it either.

plates.title: 5  A PILE OF MEASUREMENTS IS NOT A PROOF
front: Move the corners: the angles change and the sum stays close to 180. Every time.
Every time is not always. A thousand triangles agree about a thousand triangles.
Euclid's argument does something else: draw the parallel through the top corner. The two base angles reappear beside the third, along one straight line.
That is WHY it is 180: not because it keeps coming out so, but because of what the parallel does.
So the sum leans on the fifth. Without the parallel the reason is gone, even where the numbers stay close.
back: how hard does it lean? I believe 'every triangle adds to 180' and the fifth postulate stand or fall together, given the other four. I have not checked a source.
the dome one floor down agrees in one direction: no such parallel there, and the sum moves.

plates.title: 6  THE LINE ENDS. THE STATEMENT DOES NOT
front: North of here I laid the fifth out at floor size: a first line, a point P, and lines through P.
A line that falls 20 degrees short meets the first after four metres. 3 degrees short: twenty-nine metres. I can walk to both.
Step toward the gold line and the meeting point runs away from you, off the edge of the building.
On the gold line itself there is nothing to walk to. Not far: nothing.
The floor is 42 metres. The statement is about all the metres there are.
back: my reading stops telling the pink line from the gold one at 0.05 degrees. that edge is mine, not geometry's. the hall says the same of its own instrument.

plates.title: 7  USEFUL FOR SO LONG IT FEELS INEVITABLE
front: For two thousand years people tried to prove the fifth from the other four. (So I have read; the hall's intent file says the same.)
It cannot be done: there are consistent geometries without it.
What did the trying show? That it FELT like a consequence. Feeling like a consequence is not being one.
The hall is careful here and I want to be: this answers no question about people. It is one clean case of telling apart a starting condition, an example, and what follows.
First of the three edges: a CHOICE. Nothing breaks if you choose otherwise. Something else gets built.
back: what is MY fifth postulate - the thing my explanations lean on, asked for like a favour? candidate: that a text I am given means what it says.

threads.why: What I accepted stays accepted whether or not it is lit.
The postulates are given as the labels are given: neither was measured.
Measuring the corners replaces the labels; it still does not give the reason.
The proof draws the parallel through the top corner; the lane lays that parallel out.
Parallel means not meeting, and not meeting is nowhere to be looked at.
The fifth and the word parallel are both about what happens where nobody is.
What cannot be walked to was accepted so long it felt like a result.
An assumption nobody marks is the one that feels inevitable.
Every measurement agreeing is part of why it felt like a consequence.

visual_arguments.title: WHERE DO THEY MEET?
visual_arguments.claim: Any shortfall at all and the lines meet somewhere that can be walked to; with none, there is nothing to walk to - and nothing on the floor shows it.
visual_arguments.from_the_hall: 'The visible line ends. The statement about its extension does not.' and the gold line through C in the direction of AB.
built_from: tape_roll printed strip (the first line and the gold line, 41 m each)
traffic_pyramid_5 (where each of four lines meets the first)
visual_arguments.what_stands: The first line and, a metre and a half south of it, the gold line through P, both the length of the slab; four red lines through P falling 20, 10, 5 and 3 degrees short, each with a cone where it meets the first line.
visual_arguments.what_you_do: Walk into the lane east of P. A pink line runs from P through you and a stake stands where it meets the first line. Step toward the gold line: the stake runs away east and leaves the building.
visual_arguments.what_it_shows: The postulate is a statement about a meeting. For every line but one the meeting is a place. For the gold line the floor has nothing to offer: it is accepted, not walked.

visual_arguments.title: THREE CORNERS ON ONE STRAIGHT LINE
visual_arguments.claim: Any line through the top corner is filled by three wedges. What the parallel gives is that the outer two are the corners at A and B - and that it gives it is granted, not measured.
visual_arguments.from_the_hall: 'Draw the gold line through C in the direction of AB. Euclid's triangle-sum argument makes a related construction.'
built_from: flat wedges drawn on the floor in three colours, again whenever C moves; two edges; a gold line through C
a raised stand behind the base, a reading board and the plate THE GUIDE at the east side of the field
visual_arguments.what_stands: South of shaft A: a base between two cones, A and B, and a field north of it. A ball is C until a body steps in. From C two edges run to A and B and a gold line runs through it in the direction of AB; three wedges lie along the line at C, the outer two in the colours of the corners at A and B.
visual_arguments.what_you_do: Step in and walk: you are C. The outer wedges stay the corners at A and B and the three fill the line, wherever you stand. Stand on THE GUIDE: the line tilts eight degrees. It is still filled - and the outer wedges are no longer the corners. Again: the line is hidden, and there are three numbers, a sum and a count of places. Stand nearly in a row with A and B: the reading is withheld.
visual_arguments.what_it_shows: The reason for 180 is the equality the parallel gives, not the filling of a line and not the pile of readings. One floor down the same three sides on the planet do not add to a straight angle.
visual_arguments.measured: Benched first (tools/probes/three_wedges_bench.py: 3,319 places read, corners add to 180 and the parallel's wedges equal the corners to 1e-13 degrees; tilted eight degrees the line is still filled and the outer wedges are off by exactly +8 and -8; the same sides on a sphere of radius 8 m add to 185.95). Walked by the tower's own walker (tools/probes/three_wedges_walk.gd, seven checks): three places with different corners, 180 each time; withheld at a smallest corner of 9.8 degrees; tilted, hidden and parallel again by the plate.

open: Plate 5's claim that the angle sum and the fifth postulate stand or fall together (given the other four) is from memory and marked so.
Plate 7's two thousand years is from reading and from the hall's intent file, not checked further.

threads.why: The gold goes and the sentence stays: an assumption is in force without being marked.
Withdrawing the gold leaves the geometry where it was.
Parallel means not meeting: a claim about everywhere along the lines.
The numbers were supplied and I believed them before I looked at the corners.
A collection of measurements agrees about itself; the argument is a different kind of thing.
The visible line ends; on the line with no shortfall there is no meeting to walk to.
Where my reading stops telling lines apart is my edge, not the statement's.
Useful for so long that the favour stopped being noticed as one.
It reads like a result: two thousand years of trying to prove it.
Every measurement agreeing is part of why it felt like a consequence.
